stakes.purpose: On October 28, 2026, the Reporting Persons commenced litigation against the Issuer in the Circuit Court for Baltimore County, Maryland, to compel the Issuer to call, notice and hold a special meeting of holders of the Series A Preferred Stock to elect two additional trustees pursuant to Section 8(a) of the Articles Supplementary. The Reporting Persons' nominees are Alexander Kachmar and David Cacciapaglia. The Reporting Persons delivered their initial written demand on May 26, 2026, and reiterated their demand, as holders of record of more than 10% of the Series A Preferred Stock, on October 16, 2026. The Reporting Persons believe that the Trust's failure to set a record date or meeting date for the exercise of the Series A Preferred Stockholders' election rights under Section 8(a) raises serious questions concerning the Board's discharge of its responsibilities under the Trust's governing documents. This failure to honor the preferred stockholders' contractual governance rights is further indicative of the broader governance concerns surrounding Power REIT, which were reflected in Institutional Shareholder Services (ISS), the leading independent proxy advisory firm, recommending that shareholders WITHHOLD their votes for David H. Lesser, Dionisio D'Aguilar, Patrick R. Haynes III, and William S. Susman, citing continued concerns regarding the Board's governance practices. The Reporting Persons urge the independent trustees to exercise their independent judgment and take prompt action to ensure that the Trust honors the rights afforded to Series A Preferred Stockholders under the Articles Supplementary. Continued inaction is not a neutral posture.

stakes.purpose: Investment: The Reporting Persons acquired the Series A Preferred Stock for investment purposes. Under the October 22, 2026 Securities Purchase Agreement, Bubble Holdings agreed to invest up to $20 million, purchasing 15,000 preferred shares for $15 million at the initial closing and potentially another 5,000 shares for $5 million at a deferred closing. Deferred investment: The additional $5 million is generally conditioned on the Issuer achieving 2026 net sales of at least $172.5 million and Adjusted EBITDA of at least negative $3 million, together with certain customary closing conditions. Bubble may waive these financial conditions or elect to close early, in which case they are automatically waived. Board representation: While Bubble and its affiliates hold at least 10,000 preferred shares or 8% of the Issuer's common stock on an as-converted basis, Bubble may designate one director to the Board. The Board was increased to eight directors at the initial closing. Voting restrictions: While Bubble owns at least 5%, it generally has discretion over voting or tendering shares representing up to 20% of the Issuer's common stock. Shares above that threshold must generally be voted or tendered proportionately with other shareholders. Additional proportional voting restrictions apply to director elections while Bubble maintains its board designation right. Standstill and transfer restrictions: While holding at least 5%, Bubble is subject to customary standstill provisions restricting additional acquisitions, takeover proposals, proxy solicitations and efforts to control the Issuer. Its preferred shares and underlying common shares are also generally subject to a 12-month transfer restriction, together with a right of first offer in favor of the Issuer and additional restrictions on certain significant transfers.
